text:
maria: Heads-up - I ran a set of nsys captures to investigate a tail glitch after we added per-key NVTX ranges for KV cache. The capture is here: https://perfetto.dev/trace/def456. Observed some odd CPU-side work moving earlier in the timeline when NVTX count is high.

ash: Thanks. Can you summarize the key telemetry? My worry is instrumentation changing scheduling/ordering and affecting kernel selection heuristics.

maria: Quick summary from the trace: total NVTX events ~ 420k, average label length ~28 chars, CPU time spent in NVTX handling ~34ms across the run, and we see extra work inside runtime::batcher::emit_batch that correlates with the events. Also p99 latency for a 64-token batch rose ~2.6% on the canary.

jin: Minor nit on naming - let's use stable short prefixes like `rdw.kv.batch` and `rdw.kv.op`. Keeps strings compact and grep-friendly.

carmen: On batching: we currently emit one NVTX per key in a multi-key lookup. That produces N events per batch. For 64 keys it's 64 events, which is a lot. Suggest emitting `rdw.kv.batch_lookup` with a count tag and hit_count tag instead. If we need per-key detail, synthesize it offline.

perf_bot: nsys snapshot (capture 2267890123):
```
Total NVTX events: 420,216
CPU NVTX callback time: 34.2ms (serialized)
Hotspot frames: runtime::batcher::emit_batch (14.1% CPU), runtime::kernel_selector::score_candidates (9.8% CPU)
Top device kernels: attn_forward, qkv_matmul
Average label len: 28 chars
```
Perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/def456

alex: We should add two instrumenting modes: COARSE (emit batch-level ranges + metadata) and FULL (per-key ranges) behind an opt-in flag. Also add PROD_SAMPLING_RATE default 0.01 so production traces don't explode.

maria: Agreed. Also make sampling deterministic per-request (use a 64-bit hash of request id mod denom) so traces for a single request are consistent.

ash: For the COARSE mode, include fields: count, hits, batch_id(last8), and latency_ns. Keep label short; put extra data in nvtx payload if supported.

jin: If the runtime can't attach a binary payload cheaply, we can compress metadata into a short comma-separated tag `c:64,h:12,id:1a2b,lt:2400`. That keeps string length small.

carmen: One thing we noticed on the canary: kernel_selector was performing a candidate recompute right after NVTX emission. Could be lock contention from the NVTX call path. We should microbench whether NVTX calls grab any locks on the CPU path.

maria: I ran a microbench: emitting 1k coarse NVTX ranges added ~0.6ms, emitting 1k per-key NVTX ranges added ~7.6ms. So cost scales superlinearly with event count.

perf_bot: Recommendation automated: open PERF-823 to track follow-up. Attach microbench results and perfetto link.

alex: Implementation plan:
1) Add rdw.kv.{batch,op} naming scheme.
2) Implement COARSE mode that emits one range per logical batch plus compact tags.
3) FULL mode behind REDWOOD_NVTX_DEBUG only.
4) REDWOOD_NVTX_SAMPLING_RATE env var (0.0-1.0) with deterministic per-request hash sampling.
5) Add unit and perf tests: 32/64 batch microbench, measure p50/p95/p99 and CPU NVTX cost.

jin: Also add a debug endpoint to reprint synthetic per-key spans from coarse ranges (useful when investigating regressions without changing prod).

carmen: +1. For rollout, gate COARSE by default and enable FULL only on debug clusters. Run a week-long canary comparing p99 with and without instrumentation at 1% sample.

maria: I'll draft RFC + PR with benchmark numbers and the perfetto/nsys captures attached. Will include scripts to synthesize per-key spans and a short guide for search filters.

ash: Great. One last thought: add a flag to limit emission to slow requests only (e.g., emit NVTX only when latency > X ms). That reduces noise and focuses on problematic traces.

alex: Good idea. Could be REDWOOD_NVTX_ONLY_SLOW_MS.

maria: Thanks everyone. Filing PERF-823 and will ping when PR is ready. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
